subject: Values for cortical thickness in presence of atrophy/resection etc.

messages.author: 291685fb69362edf
messages.subject: Values for cortical thickness in presence of atrophy/resection etc.
parts:
Hi Chris,

I was just wondering if you had any thoughts on how completely atrophied/resected brain regions should be handled in terms of measurements of cortical thickness. For example, if I have a region of my atlas which is completely surgically resected in a patient, what should I enter in the datafile for brainGraph. Obviously the cortical thickness is zero as it does not exist, but does this then result in artificially deflating potential group-level correlations for the group? Should it instead be set to not anumber (NaN) and would brainGraph handle this is thedesired fashion of excluding that data point (not the whole subject but the region) from the group-level co variance calculations?

BW
Dan

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Values for cortical thickness in presence of atrophy/resection etc.
parts:
Hi Daniel, I would remove the subject altogether to avoid the headache, but of course if you are studying stroke patients then you wouldn't have a patient group to study! The issue is, as you mention, that some patients will be missing an entire region (or multiple); this fundamentally changes the network structure and where it "falls" among the rest of the patients. The correlations are performed by the function "rcorr" (from the "Hmisc" package), which states in its help file:

"Missing values are deleted in pairs rather than deleting all rows of 'x' having any missing variables."

So yes, I think you should set those to be NA and see if it handles them properly.

Chris
